newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate end sharply down on liquid mkt.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate end sharply down on liquid mkt.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates plunged 290 basis points to close at 18.50 percent on Tuesday due to ample market liquidity, traders said.
Dealers stressed that the final deal settled at this rate was for the relatively insignificant amount of 8.5 million pesos.
Traders nonetheless said several late deals were settled below 19 percent, and situated average trading rates for the session at 20.85 percent.

"The market felt very slack, I feel that Banco de Mexico changing the way it participates last week boosted liquidity," a dealer said, referring to the central bank's decision to raise the amount by which banks may be short in their accounts outstanding.
Traders said many brokers snapped up paper at current rates ahead of expected sharp falls in primary returns at the central bank auction to be held after the close of trade.
Dealers added that demand for paper increased market liquidity towards the close.

Analysts said Banco de Mexico participation also helped secondary rates decline. The central bank drained 2.360 billion pesos from the system through a combination of repurchase agreements and direct sales of paper.
The central bank assigned one of the repos at 19.58 percent.

Money market traders surveyed by Reuters after the central bank participation nN22536522 predicted Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 21.22 percent at the primary auction due later in the day.
This would represent a fall of 139 basis points since last week's auction.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile fell 150 basis points to 20.50 percent.
Liquidity of 3.487 billion pesos, and 600 million pesos in bank bills, were scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
